intro: Wyoming runs its elections county by county, through each county clerk.

id_rule.text: Show an acceptable ID when you vote in person. Accepted IDs include a Wyoming driver's license or ID card, a tribal ID, a U.S. passport, a U.S. military card, a driver's license or ID from another state, a University of Wyoming, community college or public school student ID, a Wyoming concealed firearm permit, or a Medicare or Medicaid card (accepted through 2029). A free Wyoming ID is available from Driver Services. If you vote absentee by mail, you do not need to send any other ID.

elections.what: Federal, state and local offices, plus any statewide or local measures. Your exact ballot depends on where you live.

dates.label: Absentee voting
dates.detail: You can vote absentee in person at your county clerk's office or by mail. Any registered voter can do this. A mailed ballot must be received by your county clerk by 7 pm on Election Day.

dates.label: Voter registration closes
dates.detail: This is the last day to register before Election Day. From Oct. 20 to Nov. 2 you can still register in person and cast an absentee ballot. You can also register and vote at your polling place on Election Day.

dates.label: Last day to get an absentee ballot
dates.detail: You can ask for a ballot any time before Election Day. A ballot can be picked up or sent any day after it is available, but not on Election Day.

dates.label: Election Day
dates.detail: Polls are open 7 am to 7 pm, and anyone in line at 7 pm can vote. Absentee ballots that arrive after 7 pm are not counted.
